latestIgtvVideos.caption: As a longtime journalist, @joannelipman is usually the one asking questions. It was fun to turn the tables and interview her about her new book “NEXT! The Power of Reinvention in Life and Work.” It's all about the lessons she’s learned throughout her career as on-air contributor at @cnbc to former Editor-in-Chief at @usatoday. In our conversation, Joanne shared her tips on how to embrace change and make the jump to a new job. I hope you check out our Q&A and pick up a copy of her book!

Like so many of you, I'm deeply saddened by the devastation and the tragic loss of life from the earthquakes in Turkey and Syria. 

@careorg is one of the heroic organizations on the ground helping Turkish and Syrian families survive.
They’re delivering critical aid including shelter, clean water, food, generators, and more. 

It was an honor to speak with Nirvana Shawky, CARE's Middle East and North Africa Regional Director, to learn about CARE’s response to the earthquake and how all of us can help the Turkish and Syrian people at this critical time.

A record number of women are running for governor in the midterms. But for these trailblazing women to get a fair chance, we need to counter unconscious bias. That means questioning our snap judgments about candidates and pushing ourselves to focus on what actually matters: their ideas and experience. Check out our @leaninorg tools to #GetOutOfTheBias at leanin.org/hear-that-say-this.

I sat down with my friend @stevecase— co-founder of AOL and renowned entrepreneur — to talk about his incredible new book, “The Rise of the Rest: How Entrepreneurs in Surprising Places are Building the New American Dream.” The book covers Steve’s 40+ city bus tour to meet with startups across the country. He shared what he saw on the tour and his advice for aspiring entrepreneurs. I hope you watch!

I grew up hearing stories from my mom about what women in our country went through before Roe. My mom had a friend who left the country to get a safe, legal abortion. Most women could not afford to do this. Some had back-alley abortions, which sometimes led to serious health complications and even death. All too often women were forced to make impossible choices between controlling their health and futures and breaking the law. Post-Roe, many more will have to make that same choice — it’s horrifying. I never thought my mom’s past would become my daughters’ futures.

Across the country, Republican lawmakers have implemented extreme or total abortion bans in 19 states — leaving 22 million women without access to abortions. @prochoiceamerica is fighting back. They are on the ground educating voters and helping to elect pro-choice candidates across the country. In my conversation with @mintimm, the President of NARAL, we discuss the impact of the Supreme Court’s ruling in Dobbs and why so much is at stake in the midterm elections.

Our daughters should have more rights than our moms had, not less. This November, we must all show up to vote to protect reproductive freedom.

It’s International #DayoftheGirl — and we should all be alarmed by the number of girls in crisis around the world. Globally more than 1 in 5 girls are married before their 18th birthday. That is one young girl married every three seconds. 

Child brides lose all control over their lives and futures. The day a girl is forced into marriage is the day her childhood ends, her education ends, and her potential is cut short. Our girls deserve more. More dreams. More hope. More opportunities. 

Together, we must stand up for the rights of girls — today and every day. And we must support organizations like @vowforgirls who are on the ground helping to stop child marriage and increase girls' access to education. Empowering girls will change our world for the better — we must give them that chance.

I grew up hearing stories from my mom about what women in our country experienced before Roe. One of her friends in college traveled to another country for a legal, safe abortion. But most women couldn’t afford to do this. Some had dangerous back-alley abortions at secret clinics. Others tried to induce abortions themselves. There was no guarantee either procedure would work. And, even if it did, women often faced serious medical complications, and many lost their lives. I cannot believe that I’m going to send my three daughters to college with fewer rights than I had. 

In the wake of the Supreme Court’s horrifying decision on Roe, more than 1/3 of women in the country have lost access to abortion. We’ve only just begun to see the devastating impact that state abortion bans will have on women’s health and their ability to determine the course of their own lives.
 
Without national protections for abortion rights, we have to take this fight to the states and to local elections. One of the organizations leading the fight is the @aclu_nationwide. They are on the ground supporting ballot measures and mobilizing voters across the United States in addition to their critical legal advocacy. In my conversation with Anthony Romero, the Executive Director of the ACLU, we unpack the Court’s ruling, discuss the ACLU’s work, and explain how you can help protect abortion rights.
 
It’s up to us to decide whether our mothers’ pasts are going to be our daughters’ futures. It’s up to us to claim back the rights that were taken from us. For ourselves, our daughters, and every generation that follows, we must protect and expand abortion access. I am so proud to support and lift up the ACLU’s important work.

I just went Live with Zweli Moyo-Williams, co-owner and chef of @zweliskitchen. We talked about her entrepreneurial journey to opening America’s first authentic Zimbabwean restaurant, and her plans to expand in Durham, North Carolina.

My niece @ellaa.goldberg and I just went Live with @drink321coffee co-founders Lindsay Wrege and Michael Evans. We talked about their incredible mission and business built on inclusion – and why it is important to them to provide meaningful jobs for adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities.

I just went Live with @marcherobinson, one of the amazing creators in Meta’s @wetheculture program. We talked about her journey to becoming a full-time creator and the inspiration behind her newly launched small business @isalinebeauty.

The Self-Employed Women’s Association in India is a wonderful example of women working together to lift each other up. It’s great to hear how they’re planning to use the new Communities feature on WhatsApp to connect with each other and their suppliers and customers in real time. We’re rolling out this feature globally later this year and I can’t wait to see how people across the world use it.

In my experience, success takes hard work, resilience, and knowing where to grab coffee.

I sleep more than I used to (thank you @ariannahuff!!) I write everything down, and I drink a lot of caffeine. These habits help me stay grounded, on track, and make steady progress — even on the busiest days.

Congratulations to my dear friend @mellodyhobson and George Lucas on the opening of the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art – a truly special place.

Mellody and George had a bold vision for a museum that celebrates the power of storytelling, and they brought it to life in such an exceptional way. I’m so grateful I had the chance to experience it – and so excited for the generations of visitors who will be inspired by the stories inside.

As the sun set last night, Jews around the world began observing Yom Kippur. The holiest day of the Jewish year, it’s a time to look inward, reflect on the past year, and commit to doing better in the one ahead.

Yom Kippur is built on a powerful idea: that we are always capable of growth. No matter our shortcomings, we can make amends and begin again. This belief — in our capacity to show up more fully for one another — belongs to no single faith. It belongs to all of us.

Wishing everyone who is observing an easy and meaningful fast. G’mar Chatimah Tovah.

Women aren’t losing their ambition. Too often, workplaces are giving them reasons to pull back.

I spoke with Business Insider about why women are stepping away from corporate leadership and what companies must do to keep them. Women need equal access to mentorship, advancement, and meaningful support at work and at home. Most importantly, they need to know their companies genuinely want them to lead.

I will always support women in making the choices that are right for their lives – whether that means pursuing a senior leadership role, starting a business, working part-time, going back to school, or staying home with their children. But those choices should be shaped by what women truly want, not by the barriers workplaces have failed to remove.

We’ve made progress, but the work is far from finished. When companies create environments where women can thrive, everyone benefits. 

Thank you to @jaypugz and @businessinsider for highlighting this important topic.

We all have too much to do – and Simplify, the new book from @axios founders @mikeaxios, @axiosjim, and @roylschwartz makes a compelling case that the answer isn’t always to do more. Sometimes, the most effective thing is doing less of what doesn’t matter, so we can do more of what does.

At a moment when AI is changing how we work this message is especially important. Technology can help us move faster, but real productivity requires clarity, focus, and the confidence to say no.

Mike, Jim, and Roy have spent their careers making complicated ideas easier to understand, and this book brings that same clarity to how we work and live. Congratulations on a timely, thoughtful, and genuinely useful book!

Every year, Rosh Hashanah asks us the same question: who do you want to be in the year ahead? 

Tom and I will gather with our children, parents, and friends to hear the shofar, dip apples in honey, and sit with that question together. There’s something powerful about doing this in community — sharing the same prayers, the same foods, the same hope that Jewish families have carried forward for thousands of years.

This year, my wish is that all of us — regardless of faith — find a moment to ask ourselves this question. And that the answers lead us toward more kindness and more compassion for one another.

Wishing everyone who celebrates a sweet new year. 
Shanah Tovah.

@fidjissimo is joining the Nscale board!!!!
 I have told the story of Facebook’s bet on mobile many times. Fidji is a big part of why that bet paid off. She built NewsFeed ads, led the video product, and then the whole Facebook app. She went on to run Instacart as CEO and Chair, took it public and made it profitable. Most recently, she ran ChatGPT and led all product and business functions at OpenAI. Fidji has spent her career at the other end of what Nscale builds — making the products that the data centers and software exist to serve. Building great products comes from being deliberate and staying close to the people you serve. No one does this better than Fidji.
 
I have had the privilege of working with many brilliant, dedicated people. Even in that talented group, Fidji stands out as a deep thinker, great executor, and truly wonderful human being.
 
Welcome, Fidji.

Grateful to take a few days away with @tom_bernthal to celebrate our 4-year anniversary.

We hiked through breath-taking forests and even spotted a mama bear and her cubs. Tom – I love adventure days – and every day – with you. ❤️

The United Nations General Assembly has adopted a landmark resolution marking November 27 as the International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early and Forced Marriage, following a push led by Sierra Leone’s First Lady, Dr. Fatima Maada Bio.

“Every instance of child marriage forecloses a world of possibilities for a young girl,” Former U.S. Secretary of State Hillary Clinton told More to Her Story following the resolution’s adoption. 

Tap the link in our bio to read the full story.

Twelve million girls are married every year before they turn 18. @firstladyfatimabio , First Lady of Sierra Leone, calls this practice what it is: “legalized rape”. 

Finally, the global community has acknowledged this scourge and taken a big step towards ending it. The first International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early and Forced Marriage — will now be observed every year on November 27. This new day gives the world an annual moment to focus on solutions: strengthen laws, share what’s working, and above all, invest in girls’ health and education so every girl can stay in school and shape her own future.

This day exists because of @firstladyfatimabio’s leadership. She has spoken with extraordinary courage about the devastating effects of child marriage — and she brought this resolution to the UN alongside leaders from Cabo Verde, Costa Rica, and Morocco and the General Assembly approved it today.

Earlier this year, I was proud to work with Dr. Maada Bio and partner with @hillaryclinton and @columbiaigp on Accelerating Efforts to End Child Marriage, a report laying out concrete steps to end this practice. 

This is what happens when women lead. Congratulations to @firstladyfatimabio and to everyone working toward a world where every girl is free to choose her own path. I hope countries around the world see this commitment and take action to strengthen their laws, protect girls, and end child marriage once and for all.

Today I join so many others in honoring the life and mourning the loss of an icon — Gloria Steinem.

I grew up admiring Gloria from afar, and later had the extraordinary honor of getting to know her. Her commitment to equality and justice for all knew no bounds and was matched only by her generosity to her friends.

As I was writing Lean In, she offered to read my drafts. She did — and sent me edits line by line — with the most generous note possible: “This is your book and my notes are just suggestions.”

That was Gloria. She spent her life making room for other women to find and use their voices, and somehow still had the ability to make you feel like yours was the one that mattered most. She didn’t just fight for a movement — she built people up, one relationship, one march, one magazine, and even one joke at a time. And she did that for nearly six decades — and right until the very end.

The world is quieter today for the loss of her voice. But so many of us carry a piece of what she gave us — so many of us know that all of our work stands on her shoulders.

Rest in power, Gloria.
